statement: We used Schnyder woods in order to prove that every (σ-)internally 3-connected graph has a 4-tree such that its co-tree is also a 4-tree. Also, we showed that there is a linear time algorithm computing such a tree. If we further relax the connectivity condition to (k-)internal 3-connectedness, then we cannot expect a 4-tree on the dual anymore. However, we always manage to find a tree such that at most one vertex of its co-tree has degree larger than 4. Grünbaum’s conjecture still remains open. We believe that it could prove worthwhile to assume further restrictions on the graph in order to decrease the maximum degree in both the tree and its co-tree or only one of them.
